title: The three sides of the aisle, and the preconditions each one requires
supersedes_reason: One evidence string carried a stale test count. The count is the evidence for a MET status, so a wrong number is not cosmetic: it is a measurement recorded wrongly. The change is to one string, but a fact with no provenance may not exist and this one had a number with no command attached, so the corrected string names the command, the working directory and the collected/passed split. The original stays on disk unedited as the record of the state before the count was verified. Authoritative pointer: the `sides` door in ai_context/systems_core/door_registry.json.
prose: Work is separated into three sides -- engine, PIP-MON in-house, and Creation Kit -- and each side has its own setup invariants. An invariant is not a capability: it is not something to build toward incrementally, it is true or it is not, and while it is false the entire side is unavailable. That distinction is the point. A capability can be partially delivered and still useful; an unmet invariant means nothing on that side works, no matter how much else is finished. The engine side currently fails at exactly one invariant, Layer A, and that single failure is why S0 is unproven, why the four testlab scripts cannot run, and why the in-engine half of the project is blocked. Everything else on that side is green. One unmet precondition is doing all the damage, which is why per-side status is reported separately and a global green gate is not permitted to imply a working side.

status_vocabulary.UNVERIFIED: Not checked. Explicitly not the same as MET.
status_vocabulary.PARTIALLY_MET: NOT IN THIS VOCABULARY. Recorded here because four entries below carry it and nothing declares it. What it is allowed to mean is not decided by this file. UNVERIFIED is not PARTIALLY_MET and MET is not PARTIALLY_MET, so an entry using it is not branchable on this vocabulary and tools/spec_lint.py does not check these entries against it. Reported, not fixed: whether a fourth status may exist is a decision for the owner, and the closure is still owed on ATTENTION.
status_vocabulary.NOT_APPLICABLE: Does not apply to this side.

sides.summary: Anything that runs inside Fallout4.exe. Papyrus, Layer A and B, the wire's engine end.
PIP-MON's own code and contracts, at either placement. Natives, the wire, the backend, the surface.
Anything at authoring time. The CK, its addons, headless xEdit, and the validation tooling.

entries.name: game and editor builds match
entries.evidence: Fallout4 and CreationKit both report 1.11.240.0; an authored plugin is rejected on load if they differ.
entries.notes: Cheap to check, expensive to ignore.

entries.name: Papyrus compiles with the real CK compiler
entries.evidence: PipMon.psc and PipMonTestFacility.psc compile via build_papyrus.bat; PipMon.pex 1034 B and PipMonTestFacility.pex 12080 B are deployed and valid.
entries.notes: Compilation is not reachability. A valid pex proves the surface is legal Papyrus, nothing more.

entries.name: every probe the surface claims resolves
entries.evidence: 18 of 18 probes resolve through Tier 1 AddressLib lookup.
entries.notes: Resolution is not dispatch. This was true while S0 was unproven, which is the proof that they are different systems.

entries.name: Layer A: the BSScript vtable slot exists
entries.evidence: No vtable slot is hooked. There is no mechanism by which a compiled .psc can reach a native we registered.
entries.notes: THE blocker. The header that holds native declarations in method order is on disk at third_party/CommonLibF4/CommonLibF4/include/RE/Bethesda/BSScript.h, with the vtable inventory beside it at third_party/CommonLibF4/CommonLibF4/include/RE/VTABLE_IDs.h. Both spellings re-verified with Test-Path on 2026-10-03, and the file is 65,388 B. VERSION 2: that sentence previously read 'CommonLibF4 RE/Bethesda/BSScript.h', which is not a path from the repo root and resolves only if you already know the CommonLibF4 root -- so the strongest lead in the project was the one thing on this entry a reader could not follow. The blocker is NOT MET and is not made closer by the header existing: the header is the lead, not the derivation, and nothing is derived from it yet.

entries.name: in-engine budget: hot path is zero-alloc and never blocks a frame
entries.evidence: No measurement exists. The constraint is documented in the tier table but nothing asserts it.
entries.notes: UNVERIFIED, not MET. A design rule nobody measures is a hope.

entries.name: telemetry ring buffer is preallocated and bounded
entries.evidence: Not implemented. The design is recorded in structural_layers.md; there is no buffer in the runtime.
entries.notes: This is what would make a verbose backend safe next to a frame-budgeted engine. Until it exists, the backend's freedom to be verbose is unmanaged.

entries.name: native table and .psc agree in both directions
entries.evidence: The self-test asserts every function declared in PipMon.psc has a matching row in the native table, and every row is declared in the script.
entries.notes: A surface in only one language is invisible or calls into nothing.

entries.name: ABI version and capability mask are defined and reportable
entries.evidence: GetVersion, GetCapabilities and GetRuntimeStatus are declared. Whether they answer is unproven, because answering requires Layer A.
entries.notes: The surface is defined; its behaviour is unproven, because answering requires Layer A. Recorded as partial so it is not mistaken for a working capability.

entries.name: the wire contract is versioned
entries.evidence: docs/IPC_PROTOCOL.md had three of ten payload sizes wrong when audited against the static_asserts. Sizes and field orders were corrected; it still documents a priority-drop scheme, a control channel and a config file that do not exist.
entries.notes: An audit found real drift, so this is recorded as partial rather than assumed good from the fact that a doc exists.

entries.name: backend is reachable, drainable, and restartable without touching the game
entries.evidence: overseer_cli runs standalone; 108 python checks pass -- `python -m pytest -q` run from overseer_cli/, which is the directory build_all.bat stage 4 pushes into, collecting 108 tests and reporting 108 passed in 0.37s on 2026-10-03 (test_detector.py 36, test_envgate.py 41, test_protocol.py 31). THE COUNT IS PATH-DEPENDENT, which is the more useful half: the identical command from the repository root collects 0 tests and errors on all three modules with ImportError, because `from overseer_cli import ...` resolves against a namespace package. So 108 is only obtainable from overseer_cli/, and a document claiming 'the python test count' without naming a working directory is quoting a number that does not exist from where the reader is standing. ai_watcher.py republishes live state to a file with a polling fallback because watchdog is absent.
provenance: python -m pytest -q from overseer_cli/, 2026-10-03: 108 collected, 108 passed
entries.notes: This is the side that is genuinely available today, and it is why the project is not starting from nothing. VERSION 2: this string read '106 python checks pass'. It was a number with no command attached, so nobody could tell a stale count from a correct one, and four documents in the tree disagreed about what the number was -- 106, 108 and 67 were all on record and only two of those three are test counts.

entries.name: CK and game builds match
entries.evidence: tools/pipmon.ps1 editor preflight compares ProductVersion for both.

entries.name: CKPE present, or an in-house replacement
entries.evidence: Absent. Three CK crash dumps are on record, and the render window crash-risks larger cells.
blocks: authoring cells larger than a handful of objects
entries.notes: CKPE is not wanted as a dependency. Eleven of its twenty techniques assess as portable and the Cell View list virtualisation is the most promising lead, but that is a candidate and not a diagnosis.

entries.name: the tool used for record work is headless and stable
entries.evidence: xEdit headless loads the full 35-plugin core and reaches Finalize at about 2m15s. It has never produced a validation report: the first attempt aborted on GetPluginName, which does not exist, and the corrected script has not yet completed a run.
entries.notes: The load is proven; the output is not. Those are different claims and only the first is established.

entries.name: the editor can be driven programmatically
entries.evidence: The CK has no scriptable interface on this machine. Every editor-facing tool is therefore read-only inspection, and authoring is manual.
entries.notes: This is why headless xEdit matters so much: it is the only route to record automation that does not require driving the CK.
